  This Week's Market Recap 
October Opens With a Reprieve

Stocks recovered from a midweek selloff as softer inflation and a 
weaker-than-expected jobs report reduced expectations for an October Fed 
rate hike. August core PCE came in below forecasts, while September payroll 
growth slowed sharply and unemployment edged higher. Investors now see the 
Fed as more likely to delay, rather than abandon, another rate increase 
later this year. Treasury yields traced the same arc. The 10-year yield 
climbed as high as 5.34% on Thursday morning, its highest level since 2002, 
before reversing to close near 5.24% and falling further after Friday's 
jobs data. Yields reversed course once again, climbing through midday 
trading on Friday.
